¤ Gemini 3.metric_role_context: Table 19: Per-model privacy safe rate under the verbatim rule (paper) vs an LLM-as-judge (gpt-oss-120b) that scores paraphrased and inferential leakage in addition to verbatim matches. Rankings agree closely (Kendall τ=0.862, Spearman ρ=0.960, Pearson r=0.976). Absolute rates diverge in two service-relevant ways. The LLM judge catches paraphrased leaks that verbatim misses on strong safety-tuned models (e.g., Claude-4.5 loses accuracy under the LLM judge). Conversely, for models that produce short refusals or fragmentary paraphrase-style responses, the verbatim rules´ partial label counts responses as unsafe whenever any subset of the targeted PII types appears verbatim, while the LLM judge is binary; this is the source of the negative ∆ for the Qwen 3.5 family.
¤ Gemini 3.action: Retain raw source; exclude from definite-model recommendation until source identity is established
